title: Migration: backfill legacy up votes (+1 -> 5, -1 -> 1), papyrus reader migrate-votes, Shipped cut-over
description:
Repo: **Papyrus**. Files: new `src/papyrus_content/reader_steering/migrate_votes.py` + `migrate_votes_test.py`; CLI command in the `papyrus reader` group (find it with `grep -rn "reader" src/papyrus_content/cli*`; follow the existing command style; writes by default, `--dry-run` reports); `features_backend/reader-steering.feature` (or a new `reader-vote-migration.feature`); `docs/reader-steering.md` (runbook paragraph).

## Change
One-shot, idempotent backfill of the ReaderVote table for a site: every row with `dimension == "up"` and `value == 1` becomes `5`, `value == -1` becomes `1`, every other row is left alone. Idempotent because a row already at 5 or 1 is never changed by the rule: run it twice, nothing moves (and a legacy `1` only exists before the first run, so the command refuses to run a second time against a table where the write path is already live unless `--force`; detect "live" as any `up` row with a value in 2..5). It pages the table through the existing store (`ReaderStore` in handler.py has `get_vote_values`/`put_vote`; add a `scan_votes` to the DynamoDB store, do not go round it), prints counts (rows seen, mapped up, mapped down, unchanged), and schedules one snapshot run at the end (`schedule_snapshot`, the debounce path) so `items.json` is rewritten once.

## Cut-over order (write it in docs/reader-steering.md and on this story when done)
1. Release with the write-path story and the snapshot story merged; deploy the site (Shipped first: it is the only site with votes today).
2. Run `papyrus reader migrate-votes --site shipped --dry-run`, read the counts, then without `--dry-run`.
3. Shipped-web ships its client change (Shipped-web story, Shipped session; reads `{mean, n, upShare}` and shows "N% up"). Between 1 and 3 the proposals page shows the old client against the new data: coordinate so the window is one deploy, or ship 3 first reading both shapes.

## Gherkin
  Scenario: Legacy up votes become five and down votes become one
  Scenario: Running the migration twice changes nothing
  Scenario: A dry run reports counts and writes nothing
  Scenario: The migration schedules one snapshot run at the end

## Acceptance
Tests pass; dry run on Shipped's table reports the expected counts, then the real run; `items.json` and the proposals data show the new shape; Shipped's proposals page shows "N% up" after the Shipped-web story deploys. Blocked by the write-path and snapshot stories and by the Shipped-web client story (external; link it here when the Shipped session files it).
